scope: Keep engine settings feedback accurate across edited drafts, configuration changes and workspace switches, and require acknowledged native credential removal.

baseline.qualification: The unconditional health completion and ignored removal acknowledgement were identified in source review. No separate pre-fix failing runtime baseline was performed for these settings changes.

prior_verification_attempts.qualification: Passed before the acknowledged-removal/failed-refresh refinement. Peer review identified an uncovered misleading-outcome path; no pre-fix failing runtime test was performed for that refinement. Original report, manifest, trace packet and log retained in dist/verification/engine-settings-before-refresh-fix.

The new post-removal UI reconfiguration used an anchored label regex that missed leading whitespace; only that locator was corrected. The unchanged restart case exhausted its cumulative 60-second budget at its second process launch, after slow startup/navigation without a failed product assertion. Timeout and assertions were retained. Complete failed reports, traces, original manifest, assessment and log are preserved in dist/verification/engine-settings-b28322b3e5b4-failure.

implementation: Bind each connection check and completed result to its tenant, draft revision, saved URL/key/revision, initialization state and connection generation; observe context transitions synchronously, including A-to-B-to-A changes.
Release an obsolete health check so a new one can run, while preventing its old completion/finally from overwriting feedback or unlocking a newer action. Ignore completion after unmount.
Explain that edited settings must be saved before testing the saved connection. Preserve newer drafts after asynchronous save completion and do not save as a testing side effect.
Use synchronous action guards and configuration pending state to prevent overlapping saves, tests and key removals. Announce current successes as status and failures as alerts.

Require trusted initialization before enqueue and again inside queued credential removal. Require a real native clear method, reject false acknowledgements, and preserve the known configured key/revision after failure; accept legacy undefined only from a real method.

Publish key removal only after acknowledgement and refresh the native connection revision. If that refresh fails after deletion, removal still succeeds with a null untrusted revision. A failed removal does not poison queued configuration changes or later retries.
Exercise deferred authenticated localhost health requests through the native app, discard the old result after a URL edit, retain the unsaved/native URL distinction, then verify a fresh check.

Verify two controlled false native removal acknowledgements retain the actual key and retry UI, then use a fresh owned process and the untouched native handler to confirm actual key removal, including after a controlled post-deletion connection refresh failure.

limitations: Packaged custom engine origins remain a source-confirmed transport gap: fixed CSP does not follow saved URLs for renderer workflow requests. This feedback change does not resolve that transport gap; a native workflow bridge including streaming is the next integration priority.
